title: Hypertension
subtitle: BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg on repeated measurements — most common CV risk factor
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- BP ≥ 140/90 on 2+ occasions, 2+ visits
- Check both arms, seated, after 5 min rest
- Target: < 140/90 (< 130/80 if diabetic/CKD)

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: FBS/HbA1c, lipid profile, creatinine/eGFR, electrolytes, urinalysis (proteinuria)
- ECG: 12-lead ECG — LVH, strain pattern, arrhythmia
- Imaging: Echocardiogram if HF suspected or uncontrolled HTN
- Monitor: Home BP monitoring, target < 140/90; renal function and K+ after starting ACEi/ARB

[TREATMENT]
- ACEi / ARB: Ramipril / Losartan — first choice
- CCB: Amlodipine — excellent for elderly
- Thiazide: HCTZ — if resistant HTN
- Beta-blocker: Bisoprolol — if tachycardia / HF

[WARNING]
Never combine ACEi + ARB — dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalemia and renal failure without benefit.

title: Stable Angina
subtitle: Chest pain on exertion, relieved by rest/nitroglycerin — myocardial ischemia
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Sternum pressure/tightness on exertion
- Relieved by rest or GTN within 5 min
- ECG may be normal at rest

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- ECG: Exercise tolerance test (treadmill) — ST depression on exertion
- Lab: Lipid profile, FBS/HbA1c, renal function — assess CV risk factors
- Imaging: Stress echo or CT coronary angiography if exercise test equivocal
- Monitor: Blood pressure, lipids, symptom frequency (angina diary)

[TREATMENT]
- First-line: Bisoprolol 5–10mg OD
- Alt (asthma): Amlodipine 5–10mg OD
- Secondary prevention: Aspirin 75mg lifelong + Atorvastatin 20mg

[WARNING]
GTN sublingual — 1 spray, repeat every 5 min up to 3 doses. If no relief → think MI → call ambulance.

⚠️↑ Myopathy risk. Prefer Fenofibrate.

Aspirin + Warfarin:
⚠️↑ Bleeding risk. Only combine under specialist supervision.

title: Heart Failure
subtitle: Dyspnea, edema, fatigue — reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- SOB on exertion, orthopnea, PND
- Bilateral pitting pedal edema
- BNP/NT-proBNP elevated — confirms diagnosis

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: BNP/NT-proBNP (elevated), renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, full blood count
- Imaging: Echocardiogram — ejection fraction, chamber size, valvular function
- ECG: Baseline 12-lead — LVH, ischaemia, arrhythmia, QRS duration
- Monitor: Daily weight, electrolytes/K+ (RAAS blockade), renal function, potassium

[TREATMENT]
- ACEi/ARB/ARNI + Beta-blocker + MRA = Foundation
- Add SGLT2i (Empagliflozin / Dapagliflozin) — mortality benefit
- Diuretic for congestion (Furosemide PRN)
- Start low, titrate to target doses — 4 pillars save lives

[WARNING]
Beta-blockers in HF: Start at lowest dose, titrate every 2 weeks. Do NOT stop abruptly. Use only Carvedilol, Bisoprolol, or Metoprolol succinate.

title: Atrial Fibrillation
subtitle: Irregularly irregular pulse — rate vs rhythm control
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Irregularly irregular pulse on examination
- ECG: absent P waves, irregular RR intervals
- CHADS₂-VASc score for stroke risk → anticoagulation decision

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- ECG: 12-lead to confirm AF (absent P waves, irregular RR); 24h Holter if paroxysmal
- Lab: Thyroid function (hyperthyroid cause), renal function, LFTs, electrolytes, FBC
- Imaging: Echocardiogram — LA size, valvular disease, LV function
- Monitor: INR (warfarin) or renal function (DOACs), heart rate, bleeding signs

[TREATMENT]
- Rate control: Beta-blocker or CCB
- Anticoagulation: DOAC preferred (Rivaroxaban/Apixaban)
- Valvular AF: Warfarin only

[WARNING]
Rate control target: Resting HR < 110 bpm. Beta-blocker or CCB — avoid Verapamil with Beta-blocker.

title: Dyslipidemia
subtitle: Elevated LDL / Triglycerides — cardiovascular risk reduction
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Low CV risk: LDL < 3.0 mmol/L
- Moderate risk: LDL < 2.0 mmol/L
- High risk (DM, PAD): LDL < 1.8 mmol/L
- Very high (AMI, stroke): LDL < 1.4 mmol/L

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: Fasting lipid profile (LDL, HDL, triglycerides), LFTs baseline before statin, renal function
- Special test: CV risk calculation (SCORE2/QRISK); HbA1c/FBS to exclude DM
- Monitor: LFTs 3 months after starting statin, then annually; lipid profile on target
- Screen: Rule out secondary dyslipidemia (hypothyroidism, diabetes, nephrotic syndrome)

[TREATMENT]
- Atorvastatin: Most potent — 20–80mg
- Ezetimibe: Add-on to statin for extra LDL reduction
- Fenofibrate: First choice for triglycerides > 500
- Check LFTs before starting

Statins + Macrolides (Clarithromycin):

⚠️ Increased Atorvastatin levels.

title: Diabetes Mellitus
subtitle: Fasting glucose ≥ 126 or HbA1c ≥ 6.5% — metabolic management
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Fasting glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL (2 readings)
- HbA1c ≥ 6.5%
- Random glucose ≥ 200 + symptoms

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: FBS, HbA1c (baseline + every 3 months), renal function, urinalysis (microalbuminuria)
- Lab: Lipid profile, LFTs (fatty liver), electrolytes — annual screening
- Special test: OGTT if diagnosis uncertain; retinal screening (annual); foot exam (monofilament)
- Monitor: Home glucose diary, HbA1c target < 7%, weight, BP (< 130/80)

[TREATMENT]
- Step 1: Metformin 500→1000mg BID + Lifestyle
- Step 2: + SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA (if HF/CKD/obesity)
- Step 3: + Sulfonylurea or DPP-4i or TZD
- Step 4: Add Insulin — start basal (Glargine)
- Target HbA1c < 7%

title: Thyroid Disorders
subtitle: Hypo- and hyperthyroidism — metabolic regulation
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Hypothyroidism: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, TSH elevated
- Hyperthyroidism: Weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, TSH suppressed

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: TSH, free T4, free T3; anti-TPO, anti-TG antibodies (autoimmune)
- Imaging: Thyroid ultrasound with scintigraphy (uptake) for thyroiditis vs nodule
- ECG: Baseline — tachycardia, atrial fibrillation (hyperthyroid)
- Monitor: TSH every 6–8 weeks to dose titrate; FBC on carbimazole (agranulocytosis risk)

[TREATMENT]
- Hypothyroidism: Levothyroxine — lifelong
- Hyperthyroidism: Carbimazole — 12–18 months

[WARNING]
Levothyroxine: Take on empty stomach, 30–60 min before breakfast. Avoid with calcium/iron supplements (space 4 hours).

title: Osteoporosis
subtitle: Reduced bone density — fracture risk in elderly
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Age > 65, female, postmenopausal
- Long-term corticosteroid use
- Low BMI, smoking, alcohol

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Imaging: DXA scan (dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry) — T-score ≤ −2.5 = osteoporosis
- Lab: Calcium, phosphate, vitamin D (25-OH), renal function, LFTs, testosterone (men)
- Special test: FRAX score for fracture risk; vertebral imaging if height loss/back pain
- Monitor: Repeat DXA at 2 years, calcium balance, adherence to bisphosphonate

[TREATMENT]
- Calcium + Vit D: Foundation — all patients
- Bisphosphonate: Alendronate 70mg weekly — first-line
- Denosumab: If refractory — subcutaneous injection

[WARNING]
Bisphosphonates: Take with full glass of water, remain upright 30 min. Avoid if GFR < 30. Risk of osteonecrosis of jaw (rare).
